title: Anthropic AI Disproves 3SUM Conjecture With New Algorithm
summary:
An algorithm discovered by an AI model refutes the APSP and Exact Triangle hypotheses and resolves the All-Pairs Shortest Paths problem in truly subcubic time. A new paper and accompanying Lean formalization claim these results disprove the Randomized Integer Word-RAM 3SUM Conjecture, which is listed as one of the most important open problems in mathematics by some LLM-based rankings.

Anthropic, the creator of the Claude model used to find the proof, employed an internal research model to certify the findings after the authors finished the initial draft. To finalize the publication, the company provided academic experts with compensation and access to Claude to assist with the write-up after identifying the proof and formalization.

selectedTweets.text:
Another amazing result (towards P=NP?), and a very interesting release scheme:

- Anthropic finds the proof together with a Lean formalization (so they know it's correct);
- They contact the experts - the authors - offer compensation and access to Claude for a help with a write-up. 

Tbh, this looks like one of the good approaches to AI-academia collaboration.
